title: Stolen Lives: Twenty Years in a Desert Jail
author: Malika Oufkir, Michèle Fitoussi
edition_analyzed: English translation, most widely read edition
target_audience: Readers interested in true survival stories
Those studying Middle Eastern and North African history
Anyone seeking insight into political repression
primary_purpose: To bear witness to the Oufkir family's ordeal of being unjustly imprisoned for two decades in the Moroccan desert as political prisoners, highlight the human consequences of authoritarian rule, and share a personal account of survival and the reclaiming of freedom.

structure_format.organization: Chronological recounting, beginning with childhood and followed by arrest, imprisonment, and eventual release
features: Detailed descriptions of daily life in captivity

key_concepts_lessons: Enduring hope is possible even in the bleakest circumstances.
Political systems can inflict devastating suffering on individuals and families.
Family love and solidarity can become a primary means of survival.
Narrative testimony helps amplify the voices of the oppressed.
The human capacity to adapt and endure can be extraordinary.
Freedom, once lost and regained, is deeply cherished.
notable_features: Based on a true account of Morocco’s most famous political prisoners
Describes not just physical endurance but psychological strategies for survival
Highlights the perspectives of women and children under political oppression
Became an international bestseller and drew attention to human rights abuses
cultural_historical_context: Set in Morocco from the early 1970s through the 1990s, the memoir reflects the aftermath of a failed coup against King Hassan II. It reveals the secretive, authoritarian nature of the Moroccan regime and brings attention to the plight of political prisoners in North Africa. The 1990s saw increasing global concern for human rights and personal narratives from non-Western settings.
reception_impact: Praised for its honesty, eloquence, and courage
Sparked international discussion on human rights in Morocco
Frequently recommended in academic settings for discussions of political repression
Some critics point to the harrowing details and unrelenting suffering as emotionally overwhelming, but most find it inspiring
